summary: Shows ansible.cfg settings for collection_skeleton and collection_skeleton_ignore (regexes on relative paths), notes that before ansible-core 2.17 only a few hardcoded variables were available, and that the default skeleton's comment_ify filter is internal.
questions: How do I set a default collection skeleton in ansible.cfg?
How can I exclude .git and other files from my collection skeleton?
Why can't I use custom variables in my skeleton on older ansible-core?
Can I use the comment_ify filter in my own skeleton?

answer_card.title: Configure collection skeleton in ansible.cfg
answer_card.answer_md:
```ini
[galaxy]
collection_skeleton = /path/to/collection_skeleton
collection_skeleton_ignore = ^.git$,^.*/.git_keep$
```
- `collection_skeleton_ignore` is a list of regexes matched against paths relative to the skeleton.
- Before **ansible-core 2.17**, only hardcoded variables (`namespace`, `collection_name`, `version`) were templated.
- `comment_ify` is internal to the default skeleton; check available plugins with `ansible-doc -t filter --list`.
